questions.q: If $C_0, C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_n$ are the coefficients in the expansion of $(1+x)^n$, then what is the value of $C_1+C_2+C_3+\ldots+C_n$ ?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following in respect of a complex number $Z$ :
1. $\overline{\left(Z^{-1}\right)}=(\bar{Z})^{-1}$
2. $Z Z^{-1}=|Z|^2$
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Let $z=x+i y, \bar{z}=x-i y$
and $z^{-1}=\frac{1}{z}=\frac{1}{x+i y}$
1. $\left(\overline{z^{-1}}\right)=\left(\overline{\frac{1}{x+i y}}\right)=\left(\overline{\frac{x-i y}{x^2+y^2}}\right)=\left(\frac{x+i y}{x^2+y^2}\right)\begin{aligned} & (\bar{z})^{-1}=(x-i y)^{-1}=\frac{1}{x-i y}=\frac{x+i y}{x^2+y^2} \\ & \therefore\left(\overline{z^{-1}}\right)=(\bar{z})^{-1}\end{aligned}$
2. $\quad z \cdot z^{-1}=(x+i y)\left(\frac{1}{x-i y}\right)=\frac{(x+i y)(x+i y)}{(x-i y)(x+i y)}=\frac{(x+i y)^2}{x^2+y^2}=|z|^2$
Hence, both (1) and (2) are true.

questions.q: The smallest positive integer $n$ for which $\left(\frac{1-i}{1+i}\right)^{n^2}$ where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \left(\frac{1-i}{1+i}\right)^{n^2}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{(1-i)(1-i)}{(1+i)(1-i)}\right)^{n^2}=1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{(1)^2+(i)^2-2 i}{1-(i)^2}\right)^{n^2}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{-2 i}{2}\right)^{n^2}=1 \Rightarrow(-i)^{n^2}=1\end{aligned}$
For $n=2,(-i)^{2^2}=(-i)^4=1$
Hence, $n=2$.

(Real)
$z-z^{\prime}=x+i y-x+i y=(2 y) i \quad$ (Imaginery)

questions.q: A ladder 6 m long reaches a point 6 m below the top of a vertical flagstaff. From the foot of the ladder, the elevation of the top of the flagstaff is $75^{\circ}$. What is the height of the flagstaff?
questions.solution:
Let $A C$ is a flagstaff of length $h \mathrm{~m}$ and $B D$ is a ladder of length 6 m . Point $B$ is below the top of the flagstaff, such that $A B=6 \mathrm{~m}$. Then, $\angle A D C=75^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned} & \text { From } \triangle A C D, \angle C A D+\angle A D C+\angle A C D=180^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D+75^{\circ}+90^{\circ}=180^{\circ} \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-75^{\circ}=15^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { As, } A B=B D \text {. } \\ & \therefore \angle C A D=\angle B D A=15^{\circ} \text { and } \\ & \angle B D C=75^{\circ}-15^{\circ}=60^{\circ} \text {. }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { From } \triangle B C D, \sin \left(60^{\circ}\right)=\frac{B C}{B D}=\frac{B C}{6} \\ & \therefore B C=6 \cdot \sin \left(60^{\circ}\right)=6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=3 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$ Hence, height of flagstaff $=(6+3 \sqrt{3}) \mathrm{m}$.

This is true for $a^2=9$ and $b^2=4\therefore \text { eccentricity }(e)=\sqrt{1+\frac{9}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (1+\cot \theta-\operatorname{cosec} \theta)(1+\tan \theta+\sec \theta) \\ & =\left(\frac{\sin \theta+\cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta}\right)\left(\frac{\sin \theta+\cos \theta+1}{\cos \theta}\right)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2-1^2}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta}\end{aligned}=\frac{1+2 \sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta-1}{\sin \theta \cdot \cos \theta}=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\cot ^2 \theta}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{1-\cot \theta}\right)^2$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{1+\cot ^2 \theta}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{1-\cot \theta}\right)^2\begin{aligned}& =\frac{1+\tan ^2 \theta}{\frac{\tan ^2 \theta+1}{\tan ^2 \theta}}-\left(\frac{1-\tan \theta}{\frac{\tan \theta-1}{\tan \theta}}\right)^2 \\& =\tan ^2 \theta-(-\tan \theta)^2=0 .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $7 \sin \theta+24 \cos \theta=25$, then what is the value of $(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 7 \sin \theta+24 \cos \theta=25 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{7}{25} \cdot \sin \theta+\frac{24}{25} \cdot \cos \theta=1 \\ & \text {Again, }(7)^2+(24)^2=(25)^2\end{aligned}\therefore$ Let $\frac{7}{25}=\cos \alpha$ and $\frac{24}{25}=\sin \alpha$
Then, $\sin \theta \cdot \cos \alpha+\cos \theta \cdot \sin \alpha=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin (\theta+\alpha)=\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \theta+\alpha=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)\end{aligned}$
Now, $\sin \theta+\cos \theta=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\alpha\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of the following?
$\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right) \sec \left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)$
questions.solution: $\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right) \cdot \sec \left(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\right)\begin{aligned} & =\operatorname{cosec}\left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \cdot \sec \left(2 \pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\ & =-\operatorname{cosec} \frac{\pi}{6} \cdot \sec \frac{\pi}{3}=(-2)(2)=-4\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $3 \cos \theta=4 \sin \theta$, then what is the value of $\tan \left(45^{\circ}+\right.\theta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 3 \cos \theta=4 \sin \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=\frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}\therefore \tan (45+\theta)=\frac{\tan 45^{\circ}+\tan \theta}{1-\tan 45^{\circ} \cdot \tan \theta}=\frac{1+\frac{3}{4}}{1-\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{7}{1}=7$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan A=\frac{1}{7}$, then what is $\cos 2 A$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\tan A=\frac{1}{7}, \cos 2 A=\frac{1-\tan ^2 A}{1+\tan ^2 A}=\frac{1-\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^2}{1+\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)^2}=\frac{24}{25}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of $\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x ?$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & y=\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d}{d x}(\sin 2 x) \cdot \cos 2 x+\frac{d}{d x}(\cos 2 x) \cdot \sin 2 x\end{aligned}=\cos ^2 2 x-\sin ^2 2 x=\cos 4 x$
For maximum or minimum value
$\frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \cos 4 x=0\therefore 4 x=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}$
Now, $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin 4 x$
At $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}, \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{2}=-4$.
$\therefore y$ is max. at $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\begin{aligned} y_{\max } & =\sin 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \cdot \cos 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \\ & =\sin \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$
